title: Last Review Before the Test: كَأَنَّ, the أَمَّا … فَـ Answer, Doubled Verbs, and the Lesson Vocabulary
summary: The final revision session reads back through the dialogues of lessons eleven and twelve, drilling the first- and second-person مُضَارِع and the feminine plural تَفْعَلْنَ. Along the way the teacher settles كَأَنَّ as another sister of إِنَّ, shows how the فَـ marks the answering clause of أَمَّا, explains why مَسْرُور traces back to a doubled verb whose two identical letters merge into a shadda, and works through the lesson's full vocabulary list of verbs and nouns.
key_points: كَأَنَّ (ka-anna : as if, it seems that) is another of the sisters of إِنَّ and carries the same rule — كَأَنَّهُمْ إِخْوَتُكَ, it seems they are your brothers.
أَمَّا is always paired: أَمَّا … فَـ …, and the فَـ marks where the answering clause begins. It cannot stand alone or form a question by itself, since as for needs something to follow.
اسْم التَّفْضِيل again: أَحْسَنُ مُدَرِّسٍ as a مُضَاف means the best teacher, while أَحْسَنُ مِنْ would mean better than — the same word carrying either sense.

عَلَامَات الاسْم (ʿalāmāt al-ism : the signs of a noun): tanwīn and أل never appear on a verb, so either one tells you at once that a word is a noun. This is the proof that a مَصْدَر such as الدُّخُول is a noun even though it conveys verbal meaning.
The مَصْدَر chain, restated: ذَهَبَ، يَذْهَبُ، الذَّهَاب; دَخَلَ، يَدْخُلُ، الدُّخُول; لَقِيَ، يَلْقَى، اللِّقَاء.

مَسْرُور comes from سَرَّ, a doubled verb whose root is really سَرَرَ — wherever a shadda appears, two identical letters have merged. أُحِبُّ is likewise أُحْبِبُ underneath, and the original letters resurface in some forms, such as the command أَحْبِبْ.

The future سَـ removes ambiguity: a bare يَذْهَبُ could mean he is going now, he goes habitually, or he will go, but سَيَذْهَبُ can only be the future. سَـ is the near future and سَوْفَ the more distant.
After يَا, a مُضَاف takes a fatḥa — يَا أُمَّ أَحْمَدَ — where a single noun would take a ḍamma.
جَمْع مُؤَنَّث سَالِم takes a kasra where a fatḥa is due, so the object in وَكَتَبْنَا الْوَاجِبَاتِ is الْوَاجِبَاتِ, not الْوَاجِبَاتَ.
صَعِدَ، يَصْعَدُ means for something to climb or rise of itself, which is distinct from رَفَعَ، يَرْفَعُ, to raise something else up.
مَاتَ، يَمُوتُ (to die) is the verb behind the noun مَوْت.
نَسِيَ is the third-person form of to forget; the book happens to list the first person نَسِيتُ (I forgot), which is unusual, since it normally gives the third-person masculine singular.

Verb vocabulary: دَرَسَ (to study), سَكَنَ (to live somewhere), شَكَرَ (to thank), نَزَلَ (to descend or get off), بَحَثَ (to search), صَعِدَ (to climb), عَرَفَ (to know), مَاتَ (to die), نَسِيَ (to forget).

Noun vocabulary: قَرِيب (close, and also a relative), عُنْوَان (address), بِطَاقَة (card), مَحَطَّة (station), ثَوْب (garment), رِسَالَة (letter), حَلَّاق (barber), مُسْتَوْصَف (dispensary), صَيْدَلِيَّة (pharmacy), أَرُزّ (rice), قَادِم (coming), فِتْيَة as the plural of فَتَى (young men), سَائِق (driver), and مُتَزَوِّج (married).

خَيْل is one of several words for horse, alongside حِصَان and فَرَس — the teacher noting that Arabs kept dozens of words for camels and over a hundred for the lion, one scholar of Lahore having written a whole poem listing them.
Schools and masjids in the Arab world are commonly named after a Companion, as with مَدْرَسَة خَالِد بْن الْوَلِيد لِلْبَنَاتِ in the dialogue.
questions: [00:14:00] Q: Can أَمَّا be used by itself as a question? — A: No. It works only in the pattern أَمَّا … فَـ …; as for cannot form a question on its own without something following.
[00:21:00] Q: Does مَسْرُور come from a verb? — A: Yes, from سَرَّ, a special type of verb whose apparent two letters are really three — the shadda marks two identical letters merged together.
[00:23:00] Q: What is the command form of أُحِبُّ? — A: أَحْبِبْ, or أَحِبَّ — the original doubled letters reappear in that form, though فِعْل الْأَمْر has not been covered yet.
[00:28:02] Q: Is صَعِدَ the same as رَفَعَ? — A: No. رَفَعَ is to raise something else up, as in raising a cup; صَعِدَ is for the thing itself to climb or rise.

[00:29:00] Q: Why does the book list نَسِيتُ rather than نَسِيَ? — A: It gives that particular form here, though normally the third-person masculine singular is listed; نَسِيَ is simply he forgot and نَسِيتُ is I forgot.
[00:30:00] Q: Why is it نَسِيتُ and not a first-person plural form? — A: نَسِيتُ is the past tense for I; the present would be أَنْسَى for I and نَنْسَى for we.
[00:34:05] Q: Should أَحْسَن here be translated as best? — A: No — she means she is better than she was before, so the comparative sense is intended.
[00:42:00] Q: Shouldn't it be الْوَاجِبَاتَ as the object? — A: It is an object, but because it is on the ـَات pattern of جَمْع مُؤَنَّث سَالِم it takes a kasra instead, giving الْوَاجِبَاتِ.

quiz.q: What does كَأَنَّ mean, and what is its grammatical behaviour?
options: Because — it takes a verb after it
As if — it is a sister of إِنَّ and puts the مُبْتَدَأ in the accusative
As for — it requires a following فَـ
quiz.a: كَأَنَّهُمْ إِخْوَتُكَ, it seems they are your brothers — one of the sisters sharing إِنَّ's rule.

quiz.q: In the pattern أَمَّا … فَـ …, what does the فَـ do?
options: It marks the beginning of the answering clause
It turns the phrase into a question
quiz.a: The teacher pointed to فَيَقُولُ in فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ as the start of the جَوَاب.

quiz.q: Which two signs identify a word as a noun rather than a verb?
quiz.a: Neither tanwīn nor أل ever appears on a verb, which is how a مَصْدَر like الدُّخُول is shown to be a noun.

quiz.q: What lies underneath the shadda in سَرَّ?
options: Two identical letters merged — the root is سَرَرَ
quiz.a: A shadda marks two identical letters pushed together, which is why the verb is really three letters, as with أُحِبُّ from أُحْبِبُ.

quiz.q: Why would someone add سَـ to يَذْهَبُ?
options: To remove the ambiguity and fix the meaning as future
quiz.a: A bare مُضَارِع can be now, habitual, or future; سَيَذْهَبُ can only be future.

quiz.q: What is the difference between صَعِدَ and رَفَعَ?
options: صَعِدَ is for the thing itself rising; رَفَعَ is raising something else
صَعِدَ is transitive, رَفَعَ is not
quiz.a: رَفَعَ الْكَأْسَ is raising a cup; إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ is good speech itself ascending.

quiz.q: What is فِتْيَة the plural of?
quiz.a: فِتْيَة is the plural of فَتَى, a young man — the word used for the group accompanying him in the dialogue.

quiz.q: Why is it يَا أُمَّ أَحْمَدَ rather than يَا أُمُّ أَحْمَدَ?
options: Because أُمّ is a مُضَاف, and a مُضَاف after يَا takes a fatḥa
quiz.a: A single noun after يَا takes a ḍamma, but a مُضَاف takes a fatḥa — the same rule as يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ.

quiz.q: Which verb is مَوْت derived from?
quiz.a: مَاتَ، يَمُوتُ means to die, and مَوْت is the noun from it.
مُسْتَوْصَف is a dispensary, distinguished in the list from صَيْدَلِيَّة, a pharmacy.

quran_examples.arabic: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هَاؤُمُ اقْرَءُوا كِتَابِيَهْ
quran_examples.transliteration: fa-ammā man ūtiya kitābahu bi-yamīnihi fa-yaqūlu hāʾumu qraʾū kitābiyah
quran_examples.translation: So as for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: Here, read my record!
quran_examples.note: The teacher's example for the أَمَّا … فَـ pattern, pointing to فَيَقُولُ as where the answering clause begins, and likening the speaker's delight to a student proud of full marks.

quran_examples.arabic: فَإِنِّي نَسِيتُ الْحُوتَ وَمَا أَنسَانِيهُ إِلَّا الشَّيْطَانُ
quran_examples.transliteration: fa-innī nasītu al-ḥūta wa-mā ansānīhu illā al-shayṭān
quran_examples.translation: Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none made me forget it except Satan.
quran_examples.note: Cited for the vocabulary item نَسِيتُ, with the teacher recounting that it was spoken by the companion of Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام about the sign they had been told to watch for.
Used to fix the sense of صَعِدَ as something rising of itself, as against رَفَعَ, raising something else.

quran_examples.translation: No! They are going to know.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's example for the near future سَـ, contrasted with سَوْفَ for the more distant future.
